discovered.name: American mahjong boom
discovered.whyConsidered: Yelp club searches reported up ~4,500% YoY, plus Eventbrite and Evite event growth, many national stories in 2026, and a clear need for learning and organizing aids.

discovered.name: Hyrox / fitness racing
discovered.whyConsidered: Reported 1.5M athletes in 2025/26 and 2M+ expected in 2026/27; training-log and race-day tracking needs line up with New Year.

discovered.name: Needlepoint revival (Gen Z stitch nights)
discovered.whyConsidered: YPulse, Fortune and CBS coverage in 2026, kits selling out, Michaels trend report; stash and project tracking need.

discovered.name: Padel (US)
discovered.rejectReason: Small committed base (238K played 8+ times, reported), about 40% of courts in Florida; gift demand is gear-led (grips, balls, bags) and no evidence of printable or tracker demand was found. Watch for 2027.
discovered.whyConsidered: PadelUSA-reported 1.07M US players in 2025 and 1,000+ courts by April 2026 (padelusa.org, padelbrowser.com).

discovered.name: App-driven birding (Merlin/eBird)
discovered.rejectReason: Strong newcomer data, but life-list journals and logbooks are well supplied by established publishers and books (Insight Editions' 'The Bird Watcher's Journal'; 'The Birder's Logbook'; beginner field journals) and $0.99 printables; no clear gap for a new seller.
discovered.whyConsidered: Merlin reported 16.3M active users in 2025 (+35%) and nearly 100% growth during the 2026 Great Backyard Bird Count (birdcount.org, charlottenewsvt.org).

discovered.name: Backyard chickens
discovered.rejectReason: Coverage of the newcomer surge is concentrated in Feb-Jun 2025 around the egg-price spike; no 2026 acceleration found. Chicken-keeping journals are a common KDP genre (not verified this session).
discovered.whyConsidered: APPA-cited ~11M US households keeping chickens; surge tied to bird-flu egg prices (fortune.com 2025-02-13, abc7news).

discovered.name: Run clubs / social running
discovered.rejectReason: The growth is social, not about tracking (Strava itself is the log), and running logs and training journals are a long-saturated category (inference).
discovered.whyConsidered: Strava reported new clubs nearly quadrupled in 2025 and run clubs are now the main entry point (sgieurope.com, athletechnews.com).

discovered.name: Rucking
discovered.rejectReason: Growth evidence is old (Strava 2021 +40%, Instagram 2023 +150%); 2026 coverage is one syndicated explainer, and the activity needs little tracking or content.
discovered.whyConsidered: 2026 NPR beginner's guide syndicated widely (wfae.org, tpr.org 2026-02-11).

discovered.name: Smart telescopes (Seestar etc.) as a new consumer tech habit
discovered.rejectReason: Insufficient evidence: only buying guides and Black Friday deals found, with no participation or sales figures showing a newcomer influx.
discovered.whyConsidered: Cheap app-controlled telescopes since 2023 (astrobackyard.com, digitalcameraworld.com); observing-log and target-list product idea.

discovered.name: Coin collecting: 2026 Semiquincentennial quarters + end of penny production
discovered.rejectReason: Timely, but physical folders and rolls from the US Mint, Littleton and others cover the obvious need better than a printable; evidence of the newcomer surge comes mainly from industry press and dealers. Watch for a kids' 'coin hunt' logbook angle.
discovered.whyConsidered: Five one-year-only 2026 quarter designs (Gettysburg Address quarter expected late Oct 2026), penny production halted in 2025, and dealers reporting new collectors (coinworld.com, numismaticnews.net, koamnewsnow.com).

discovered.name: Kitchen witch / herbal apothecary (Pinterest 2026 Hobbies Report)
discovered.rejectReason: Belief-adjacent with herbal-remedy health-claim risk; the obvious products (apothecary labels) overlap with saturated Halloween witchy decor; Practical Magic IP is off limits.
discovered.whyConsidered: Pinterest reported 'herbal apothecary' searches up 595% (May 2025 vs May 2026), tied to Practical Magic 2.

discovered.name: Fibermaxxing
discovered.rejectReason: Nutrition/health-claim risk; trackers and 30-day workbooks already sold (Gumroad 'Fiber Fix 30', Payhip playbook) plus apps; the trend has run since 2025 and may be peaking.
discovered.whyConsidered: TikTok nutrition trend; Whole Foods named it a 2026 trend; tracker need (2minutemedicine.com, gdruk.com).

discovered.name: Dumbphones / digital detox
discovered.rejectReason: A real behavior shift, but the purchase is the device or service; no evidence found that people want detox trackers or printables, and the theme is a broad category, not a specific hobby.
discovered.whyConsidered: Fortune (2026-04-01) on a $5B Gen Z analog economy; Axios (2026-05-07) on Gen Z leaving social media.

discovered.name: Adult Pokemon TCG collecting
discovered.rejectReason: High IP risk (names, artwork, set data) and collection tracking is dominated by free apps and price trackers.
discovered.whyConsidered: Pokemon TCG estimated at $2.7B in annual sales; Circana: 19% of US adults bought cards for themselves (10news.com, vtmvending.com).

discovered.name: Birthday magazine templates
discovered.rejectReason: A one-off gift project rather than a hobby with a newcomer base, and editable templates are already widely sold (Gumroad, Getly).
discovered.whyConsidered: Pinterest 2026 Hobbies Report: 'making a birthday magazine' searches up 1,713%.

discovered.name: Junk journaling
discovered.rejectReason: Mature, heavily supplied Etsy category (ephemera kits, printables); 63% growth on a large base gives a new seller little room (inference; not checked this session).
discovered.whyConsidered: Michaels reported junk-journaling searches up 63% YoY.

discovered.name: E-ink tablet templates (reMarkable, Kindle Scribe, Boox)
discovered.rejectReason: Market-size figures came only from low-reliability aggregator pages (alibaba.com, accio.com), and template sellers (e.g., templacity.com) already occupy the niche.
discovered.whyConsidered: A new consumer tech habit with demand for PDF planners and templates.

discovered.name: Tarot for beginners
discovered.rejectReason: Belief-based, outside this lens, and tarot journals are a crowded genre (inference).
discovered.whyConsidered: Pinterest reported 'tarot cards for beginners' up 558%.
